title: Flush IP addresses from a network interface
summary: Remove all IP addresses in a specific scope from a network interface. This is often used to reset an interface's configuration.

steps.explain: Delete all IP addresses in the 'global' scope from a network interface. Requires root privileges.
steps.cmd: sudo ip address flush <INTERFACE> scope global

rollback.explain: There is no direct command to restore flushed addresses. You must manually re-add them using 'ip address add' or restart the network service.

warnings: Flushing addresses will disconnect the interface from the network.
Ensure you know how to restore connectivity (e.g., via DHCP or manual configuration) before flushing.
